key_insight: Standardizing prostate cancer EHR data to OMOP and adding NLP plus PSA-based rules substantially improved capture of key clinical details and missing outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This approach can make real-world prostate cancer datasets more complete and research-ready while also helping identify gaps in registry data.
method: Transformed UTMB Epic EHR data (2010–2021) into OMOP CDM v5.4.
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical notes.
Applied PSA-based algorithms to find missing treatment details and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: Of 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with the cancer registry, PSA agreement was excellent, and NLP markedly improved sparse Gleason and stage capture.
watch_item: Structured EHR fields were incomplete and some improvements relied on manual review and algorithmic inference, so external validation is needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
